SK2093 The handler discards the exception it caught

The catch names the exception, throws a different one, and never passes the first to the second.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

catch (SqlException error) { throw new ImportException("the import failed"); } keeps the word "failed" and throws away the stack trace, the message, the error code and the cause. The caller is handed a sentence it cannot act on, and the frame that actually broke is no longer in the process. It looks like diligence, which is why it is more common than either the empty catch SK2014 reports or the throw ex; restatement SK2015 reports — and the repair is one argument.

Example

Instead of:

catch (SqlException error) {
    throw new ImportException("the import failed");
}

Write:

catch (SqlException error) {
    throw new ImportException("the import failed", error);
}

When it does not fire

⚠ Not `SK2014`. That rule reports a catch whose block is empty, and its negative fixture asserts silence on any clause containing a statement; this one requires a statement, so the two cannot both fire on one clause. ⚠ Disjoint from `SK7092` by construction rather than by filter. SK7092 requires the clause to propagate what it caught, by throw; or throw error;; this rule requires that it does not. The two conditions are negations of one another, so no clause can produce both findings and no supersedes entry is involved. ⚠ The rule ships the half it can repair and names the half it omits. A finding needs a catch that declared a variable — the author's own statement that the exception mattered — and a replacement type that already offers a constructor taking the same arguments plus a trailing System.Exception. Where no such constructor exists there is no edit to propose and the advice would be to redesign a type the handler's author may not own; where the clause binds no variable, catch (FileNotFoundException) { throw new ConfigMissing(...); } is a deliberate translation in which the type was the whole of the information. Passing the caught exception anywhere inside the construction — as the inner exception, or interpolated into the message — is silent, as is a throw inside a nested try/catch, a lambda or a local function. The fix appends the caught variable as the trailing argument and is fixIsSafe: false: it changes what a caller sees, and a boundary that deliberately hides the cause from an untrusted consumer is the one shape where the finding is right about the mechanism and wrong about the intent.
